testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the air compressor connected to?
questions.explanation: The air compressor connects to the engine using gears or a belt. It can be cooled by air or by the engine's cooling system.

questions.question: When should air tank drains be used?

options.text: Only when it is wet outside.

questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from the tanks. Always drain the tank completely when using the drain.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: They are not allowed on vehicles.
They hold compressed air for the brakes.
They should be emptied after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air that the brakes use. The number and size of tanks varies by vehicle.

questions.question: What do the air storage tanks hold?

options.text: Enough air for only one brake use.
Enough air for the brakes to work several times even if the compressor stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Enough air for the brakes to work several times even if the compressor stops.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks store compressed air for braking. They hold enough air so the brakes can still work several times if the compressor fails.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns in a brake drum, what does it do?

options.text: It presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
It presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
It presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: Do not drive if a brake drum has a crack larger than what fraction of the friction area width?
questions.explanation: Check brake drums before every trip. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack bigger than one half the width of the friction area.

questions.question: What should turn on automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi?
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Chock the wheels and step on the brake pedal several times to release air. The parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should turn on.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning comes on while driving a vehicle with air brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Test the brakes while driving and continue if they seem okay.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and park the vehicle as soon as you safely can. You must stop while you still have some braking power left.

questions.question: What prevents air from escaping if the air compressor leaks?
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is required between the air compressor and the first main tank. It stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: What should be done with water and compressor oil found in the compressed air?

options.text: They are needed for the system to work properly.
They should fill about 10 percent of the tank.

questions.explanation: Water and compressor oil build-up can damage an air brake system. Air storage tanks have drains to remove this build-up. Use manual drains at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake has a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to apply the parking brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: What should air tank drains do?

options.text: Not be used by the driver.
Only be used when it is wet outside.

questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. You must open the manual air tank drains every day to remove this build-up.

questions.question: What shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells you how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: What is usually found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. You must drain the tanks regularly to remove this build-up.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks. It stops pumping when pressure gets too high and starts pumping when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997, and other vehicles with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1998, must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: While going downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is:
questions.explanation: While driving downhill, hold the brake pedal down until your vehicle slows to 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when the spring brakes are on. Using both together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When should manual air tank drains be opened?

options.text: Never — they should be sealed with glue.

questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. You must open the manual air tank drains every day to remove this build-up.

questions.question: When should you avoid using the parking brake?

options.text: When the brakes are very hot.
When the brakes are very cold.
When there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake right after coming down a steep grade if your brakes are hot. Let your brakes cool first to avoid damaging them.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems add alcohol to the system?

options.text: To stop the brakes from squeaking.
To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
To prevent people from breathing the air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to stop ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum safe leakage rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not exceed 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before each trip, check each slack adjuster. Park the vehicle, set wheel chocks, and release the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to make sure it moves no more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, what should you do?

options.text: Use the parking brake only if the vehicle is parked on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake, as it can damage the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When used and maintained correctly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.
